summary: Uncommitted pin state after canary cutover blocks routing to newly promoted model variant
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary promote for BrightBank's tenant route, a subset of edge nodes retained a pre-commit pin-state which prevented them from accepting the promoted variant. Traffic that hit those nodes was transparently diverted to an older (legacy) variant, causing mixed-model outputs and a spike in inference cost. The canary controller reported a successful promote, but route routing tables on ~12% of the edge pool never completed the final pin commit step.

Impact:
- Customer-facing production traffic for BrightBank returned mixed responses (new and legacy variant) for ~18 minutes.
- Two downstream services observed quality regressions and automated validation alarms fired.
- Billing showed a temporary cost increase due to longer tail-latency and degraded cache reuse.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) dedicated tenant for BrightBank, enterprise plan with pinned model policy.
- Canary rollout window 03/10 02:40–03:05 UTC.

Observed indicators: 
- Orchestrator logs show promote commit acknowledged by control plane at 02:53:18 UTC.
- Edge proxy metrics: a cluster of nodes (agent shard 7/12) continued to report model_pin_state=PRECOMMIT.
- Router metrics show 12% of requests hit legacy variant; 88% hit promoted variant.
- No explicit 5xx errors, but client-side QA checks flagged content drift and triggered alerts.

Why this is different from a typical fallback: the system did not intentionally fallback for health reasons — it faithfully routed based on stale pin state on certain edge nodes.
steps_to_reproduce: Schedule a canary promote for a tenant with explicit pin policy (use BrightBank tenant config).
Simulate uneven edge propagation by introducing a 30s jitter to orchestrator -> edge commit messages on a subset of shards.
Send steady traffic from multiple tenant sessions and observe routing percentage splits in the routing dashboard.
Verify edge nodes with delayed commit retain model_pin_state=PRECOMMIT and continue serving legacy variant.

comments: 2026-03-10 03:10 — Support (Aisha): Customer reported mixed outputs; initial mitigation request is to force pin to legacy variant while we investigate.
2026-03-10 03:18 — SRE (Marco): Identified group of edge nodes with PRECOMMIT state; orchestrator acked commit but edge did not transition. Investigating commit delivery/logging plumbing.

2026-03-10 03:35 — SRE (Marco): Applied temporary routing rule to exclude affected shards from BrightBank route (edge- shard filter). Traffic now 100% to promoted variant after drain; monitoring for regressions.

2026-03-11 09:05 — Eng (Lina Zhou): Reproduced in staging by delaying commit receipts; appears race between commit apply and cache warm prewarm step causes rollback to PRECOMMIT in some code paths. PR linked for a guard: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/4123
2026-03-12 12:00 — Support (Aisha): Customer accepted temporary mitigation; requesting postmortem and permanent fix ETA.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Orchestrator delivered commit, but edge apply path failed due to interleaving with prewarm/cache init resulting in an interrupted state machine transition.
Hypothesis 2: A rare edge-side exception during TTL refresh caused rollback to PRECOMMIT; exception suppressed by catch-all which did not move state forward.
Telemetry: Correlated exceptions from edge shard 7 between 02:53:40–02:54:00 UTC showing 'kvcache-init-timeout' and 'state-machine-interrupt' traces.
Risk vector: This can cause silent mixed-variant behavior without 5xxs, making detection reliant on QA/validation checks or routing percentages.
resolution: Workaround applied: excluded affected edge shards from routing for BrightBank and rerouted traffic to healthy shards while we patched the apply path. Engineering deployed a guard in staging to ensure commit->apply becomes an atomic transition (PR #4123). Next steps: code review and deploy guard to production, add monitoring alert for pin_state drift >5% per tenant, and add end-to-end test for delayed commit handling. Customer notified and workaround accepted. ETA for prod fix: 2026-03-15.
next_steps: Merge and ship PR #4123 to prod (owner: Lina Zhou).
Add a post-deploy canary to catch pin_state divergence (on-call SRE to validate).
Create automated test that simulates delayed commit delivery to edge and verifies final pin_state consistency.
Run postmortem and share with BrightBank and internal stakeholders; include mitigation timeline and monitoring changes.
